segments.content:
Chapter 214 The Han-Bai Dispute

"Future Era" is benchmarked against "Dungeon & Fighter."

"Dungeon & Fighter" was developed by a small company and severely lacked marketing and promotion funds during its initial launch in South Korea. But it spread rapidly purely by word-of-mouth, and has now become the fourth most-played game in South Korean PC bangs.

In this day and age, Korean games are popular throughout East and Southeast Asia.

"DNF" has broken into the top four in Korean PC bangs, and could break into the top three at any moment. How could Chinese and Japanese game companies ignore it?

Currently, the Korean side is already in contact with Japanese distributors. Once the Japanese distribution rights are settled, they will contact Chinese game companies.

The news of "DNF's" explosion in popularity in Korea put some pressure on Chen Guiliang, prompting him to visit Youke's Future Studio every two or three days.

He couldn't help with the technical side, but he could offer opinions on the plot and art style.

The studio currently had three artists, who had already designed numerous characters, items, and scenes. Chen Guiliang would occasionally drop by to boss them around.

The art style of "DNF" went through several periods, being quite crude in its early days.

Chen Guiliang directly used the mid-period art style of "DNF" as a requirement for the artists at Future Studio.

"Boss, my classmate Feng Ji is here."

"Bring him in."

Feng Ji had been living in Jiangcheng for over a year, originally renting a place off-campus to study for the graduate entrance exams. But he ended up blowing through his entire year's living expenses and even borrowed 8,000 yuan from his roommate. That rented apartment became a pit stop for gaming.

He didn't look sloppy at the moment; he had even gotten a haircut for the occasion, and his clothes were clean.

"Do you have any money on you?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"I do." In reality, Feng Ji only had a little over 100 yuan left.

Moreover, he had already found a job in Jiangcheng as an event planner for a small game company. But before he even started, he heard he could get into Youke, so he quickly bought a train ticket to the capital.

Chen Guiliang conducted the interview himself: "What are your thoughts on free-to-play games?"

Feng Ji answered immediately: "Free-to-play games are killing the Chinese online game market."

The classmate who recommended him was so frightened he blinked repeatedly, signaling Feng Ji not to speak recklessly.

Because "Future Era," which Youke was developing, was a free-to-play game, and "Sovereign of the World," which Chen Guiliang invested in, was also a free-to-play game.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Then you'll have to bear with it, as you're about to participate in the development of a free-to-play online game."

"Huh?" Feng Ji's mouth hung open, not knowing what to say next.

Chen Guiliang said, "Go handle the onboarding procedures. You'll have a one-month probation period with the standard probationary salary. Within this month, you need to find a suitable position for yourself in the studio. Then we'll sign a new contract to make you a full-time employee."

"Okay, thank you, Boss." Feng Ji was led by his classmate to take care of the paperwork.

Chen Guiliang wandered around Future Studio for a while, then headed over to the Legends of the Three Kingdoms team.

To celebrate World Online Game Day, the Legends of the Three Kingdoms team was planning an event, taking the opportunity to release some special "Three Kingdoms Show" customizations and general skins.

Xu Fengyin was completely absorbed in her drawing. After finishing a section, she reached for her water cup, only to find it had long been empty. She stood up to get some water and was startled to find Chen Guiliang standing behind her. She patted her chest and said, "Why are you like a ghost... you don't make a sound when you walk?"

"You carry on." Chen Guiliang had just been admiring the busty Cai Wenji.

Currently, the generals in "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" included the Standard, Wind, Fire, and Forest expansion packs.

The Mountain, Yin, and Thunder packs, as well as later generals, had not been released yet.

However, during the Spring Festival, a single general from the Mountain pack, Zuo Ci, had been released.

In the upcoming World Online Game Day event, the rest of the generals from the Mountain pack would all be released.

Chen Guiliang admired Cai Wenji for a while longer, then strolled over to Qu Guohao.

Qu Guohao said, "JJ Lin's agent called us yesterday,主动 to lower the endorsement fee to 5 million. And that's the total endorsement fee for mainland China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, including the rights to use his song 'Cao Cao' for online game-related products."

"That shows some sincerity," Chen Guiliang said. "Get Chinese Gamer International to join the discussion. We've given them the distribution rights for Legends of the Three Kingdoms in Hong Kong, Macau, and Taiwan. We can discuss splitting the endorsement fee. We still need to press the price down a bit more."

"I've already contacted Chinese Gamer International. They've agreed to participate in the subsequent negotiations," Qu Guohao said.

After discussing distribution rights, they moved on to the market.

Qu Guohao said, "Legends of the Three Kingdoms is a puzzle-type casual game. And a big shark has just entered the casual game market. 'Crazyracing Kartrider' was in closed beta for two months before, with only three servers open the whole time. Now it's in open beta, and it hit 120,000 concurrent users in three days. It'll probably break 200,000 in a few more days."

"Don't worry, Legends of the Three Kingdoms just needs to hold steady," Chen Guiliang said.

Chen Guiliang never worried about the longevity of "Legends of the Three Kingdoms." It could outlast countless other games while still thriving. It would ultimately become a one-of-a-kind marvel in the gaming world!

It even reached a point where any trash game appearing on Steam would scare countless Legends of the Three Kingdoms fans into emerging. They would all arrange to go give "Legends of the Three Kingdoms" a negative review, lest the new trash game threaten its throne as the worst-rated.

When Chen Guiliang was leaving Youke, he ran into Feng Ji, who was photocopying his documents. He said, "Go get a thousand-yuan advance on your salary and rent a place first. I've already spoken to them about it."

"Thank you, Boss." Feng Ji thought this CEO Chen was a really good guy; he was indeed very short on money right now.

Chen Guiliang timed his bike ride back to the university, arriving at the classroom for the last class of the morning just in time. After class, he could go straight to the cafeteria for lunch.

He had developed a habit now. No matter how busy he was, he would attend at least two classes.

One reason was to stay in touch with university students, and the other was that listening to lectures could stimulate his thinking.

"Chen Guiliang!" The Yuanpei Program's athletics representative, Xia Hui, called out to him.

Chen Guiliang smiled. "Lao Xia."

Xia Hui asked, "The university sports meet is next month. Do you want to sign up for anything?"

"I think I'll pass. My physical fitness is pretty average," Chen Guiliang said.

Xia Hui said, "You skipped last year. This year, you have to at least join the tug-of-war, right?"

Chen Guiliang thought for a moment. "Alright."

Xia Hui added, "Tug-of-war requires training too. How to breathe, how to exert force, how to shout the rhythm, all these things need practice. Starting this weekend, all the way until the sports meet, we'll have one hour of training every weekend."

"Okay, please give me a call ahead of time when it's time for training," Chen Guiliang said.

"That's great," Xia Hui was overjoyed. "I knew you hadn't strayed from the masses. If you're willing to sign up, the other students will definitely be enthusiastic about signing up too!"

Chen Guiliang thought it was a good idea.

Participating in group activities once in a while would prevent him from forgetting that he was still a student.

After listening attentively to the class, Chen Guiliang rode his bike to the cafeteria, had a full meal, and slowly returned to his dorm.

Then he sat down at his computer to write.

The fourth volume of "Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty," which he had been dawdling on for over a year, was finally nearing completion.

As for the fifth volume, he'd have to see about it later. Who knew when he could write it.

Researching materials took too much time!

As he clattered away on the keyboard, his two junior roommates came in, happily carrying a computer.

"Congratulations, congratulations," Chen Guiliang said.

Tong Zhihong was quite proud. "I built this computer myself. No money from my parents, and I didn't use the reward for getting into Peking University. I earned it all myself by tutoring."

Li Heng said, "I'm planning to buy a second-hand one. I've already posted a request on Kaixin Market."

"Where's Senior Brother Jiang?" Tong Zhihong asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Probably on a date. He and that girl from the physics department are officially a couple now."

Chen Guiliang typed the last character of the fourth volume of "Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty," then rubbed his sore wrists and let out a long sigh of relief.

He wouldn't send the manuscript to Li Xunhuan just yet. Chen Guiliang was becoming more and more protective of his reputation, afraid of making any common-knowledge mistakes. So, before publication, he still needed to have it reviewed by a Ming history expert. Since he was at Peking University, it was very convenient to ask a professor.

Tong Zhihong and Li Heng had already set up the computer and connected the network cable, and were downloading various applications and games.

Chen Guiliang glanced over. "Download 'Legends of the Three Kingdoms' first. What are you downloading 'World of Warcraft' for?"

"Hehe." Tong Zhihong chuckled awkwardly.

Chen Guiliang sent the manuscript of "Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty" to Professor Wang's email, then called him respectfully to ask for his critique.

Finally done with that, he logged into Kaixin001 and Hainei.

The website's name was currently in a transitional phase.

Chen Guiliang posted a message: "The fourth volume of 'Those Happenings in the Ming Dynasty' is finally finished. Friends, please stop rushing me. I will try my best to speed things up."

Soon, users who followed him replied:

"You dragged it out for over a year, have you no shame?"

"Who's with me to go to Peking University and snatch the manuscript? Type if you're in."

"I'm in! I'm in the capital, very close to Peking University."

"Death to the slacker author!"

Chen Guiliang chuckled as he read the comments, then went to the new users page.

The latest one hundred registered users would be displayed. Half were regular users, and half were real-name verified users.

Many users liked to refresh this thing to see which celebrities had joined.

Chen Guiliang spotted Wang Shitou of Vanke at a glance. He was someone that ByteDance had proactively invited. At first, Wang Shitou hadn't intended to agree, but when he heard Chen Xiaoxu had joined, he readily registered an account too.

"Senior Brother, why aren't you writing articles to join the war of words?" Tong Zhihong was still downloading "World of Warcraft." It was going to take a while, so he decided to browse some blogs.

For the past half a month, Sina Blog had been generating a lot of buzz.

The Han-Bai dispute had begun!

It started when the traditional writer Bai Ye wrote a blog post evaluating post-80s writers, in which he specifically criticized Han Han.

Han Han quickly responded with a piece: "The Literary Circle is Bullshit, Nobody Should Act High and Mighty."

Bai Ye used Han Han's article as evidence of the poor character of the post-80s generation and wrote another blog post in response.

Han Han fired back again. And his cannon fire was fierce, exposing Bai Ye's academic corruption, such as self-promotion and accepting money from people.

In particular, a reporter had once fabricated a post-80s writer, and Bai Ye had claimed, "I've read this writer's articles. They're average and still need work." Han Han dug up this incident as well.

Bai Ye was infuriated and shut down his blog directly.

The war of words between these two main figures had ended, but the real battle had just begun. A large group of celebrities from the literary and arts circles launched a siege against Han Han on their blogs.

This included the likes of Ai Dajin and the Lu Tailang father-son duo.

As more and more literary and arts celebrities joined the fray, Sina Blog's popularity soared, and its market share increased by at least 5%.

Chen Guiliang said, "What does their feud have to do with me?"

Chen Guiliang had no interest in the Han-Bai dispute.

If he helped Han Han curse people now, in just a few years, that guy would bury the hatchet with Ai Dajin and Lu Tailang with a smile. Hey, those few would end up hanging out together.

Tong Zhihong said, "Don't you know? Before Bai Ye closed his blog, he did a media interview and bad-mouthed all post-80s writers. Including you."

"He flew into a rage and accidentally fired off an AoE attack," Chen Guiliang said. "If I were to join the war of words now, it'd be like watching dogs fight on the roadside. One of the dogs barks at the roadside a couple of times, and then I rush over to bite that dog. That's just degrading!"

Tong Zhihong thought about it. "That's true."

Chen Guiliang logged out of his account and lay down on his bed for an afternoon nap.

Li Heng immediately sat down at the computer and started happily making spoof videos.

His phone vibrated with a text message.

Chen Guiliang picked up his phone and saw it was from Tao Chenggang: "Those VCs couldn't agree on Balian Technology's valuation and almost got into a fight. I overheard it."

(End of this chapter)
